item.title: A Proof of a P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} Conjecture: A PDE Approach to Capacity Inequalities
item.description:
arXiv:2611.26633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a planar capacity-ratio inequality conjectured by Polya and Szego, together with its extension to adjacent dimensions: for every integer $n\geq2$ and compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $C_{n-1}(K)\leq \left[ rac{\Gamma(n/2)}{\sqrt\pi \Gamma((n+1)/2)}ight]^{1/(n-1)}C_{n-2}(K),$ where $C_s$ denotes the length-homogeneous Riesz capacity and, when $n=2$, $C_{n-2}=C_0$ is logarithmic capacity. Closed balls attain equality, so the constant is sharp. Starting from an exterior Dirichlet problem and its nonnegative boundary flux, we construct a function $ho$ in one higher dimension, with coordinates $X=(x,z)$, and prove that, for $z
e0$, $\Deltaho= rac{n-1}{ho}|
ablaho|^2+ rac{ho_z}{z}, \quad ho|
ablaho|^2\leq(ho^2-1) rac{ho_z}{z}.$ A decreasing function $\Phi_n$ solving a suitable ordinary differential equation makes $U=\Phi_n(ho)$ superharmonic outside the conductor. Green's formula on the exterior of level sets of $U$ then bounds the Dirichlet integral by the total flux at infinity, and the Dirichlet principle yields the capacity bound. Smooth outer approximation extends the result to arbitrary compact sets. The same construction, combined with a comparison principle for weighted elliptic equations, gives the sharp upper bound for $C_q/C_{n-2}$ when $n-2<q<n$.

item.title: A rigorous Abel-summed Hardy-type identity for $p$-circle domains via regularized Poisson summation
item.description: arXiv:2611.26769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our previous work, a generalized Hardy-type identity (GHI) for astroid-type $p$-circle domains was formally derived in terms of generalized $p$-Bessel functions. However, the direct application of the Poisson summation formula to the indicator functions of these domains leaves the convergence and rigorous justification of the resulting oscillatory series unresolved. In the present paper, we address this difficulty by introducing an anisotropic regularization based on convolution kernels with Fourier multipliers $e^{-t(|\xi_{1}|^p+|\xi_{2}|^{p})}$. We establish the corresponding regularized Poisson summation identity and rigorously justify the limiting process through uniform estimates for lattice-point sums. A key feature of our analysis is the determination of boundary contributions: smooth boundary points carry weight $1/2$, whereas the contributions from axial cusps vanish for $0<p<1$. These results lead to an Abel-summed GHI, expressed in terms of the distorted-angle-dependent $p$-Bessel functions introduced in our previous work, with explicit boundary corrections. In particular, for $p=2$, the identity recovers the Abel-summed form of the classical Hardy--Vorono\"i Bessel series. Our result provides a rigorous regularized counterpart of the previously proposed identity, while the convergence of the corresponding unregularized series remains a separate problem.
item.dc:creator: Masaya Kitajima

item.title: A periodic Ambrosetti-Prodi problem with sign-changing nonlinearities
item.description: arXiv:2611.27254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the periodic solutions of the second-order equation \begin{equation*} u''+f(t,u)=s, \end{equation*} where $s\in\mathbb{R}$ is a parameter and $f$ is periodic in the time variable and satisfies the one-sided sublinear growth condition \begin{equation*} f(t,x)\geq a(t)|x|^p+b(t), \qquad 0<p<1, \end{equation*} for some $a,b\in L^1([0,T])$ with $\int_0^T a(t)\,\mathrm{d}t>0$. We establish an Ambrosetti--Prodi type theorem: there exists a threshold $s_0\in\mathbb{R}$ such that the equation has zero periodic solutions for $s<s_0$, at least one for $s=s_0$, and at least two for $s>s_0$. The main novelty of our result is the removal of the non-negativity assumption on the weight $a$, which is replaced by the weaker requirement of a positive mean value, thus allowing for sign-changing nonlinearities.
item.dc:creator: Marzio Bona, Guglielmo Feltrin

item.title: The Ritt problem is decidable
item.description: arXiv:2611.27008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an affirmative solution to the Ritt problem.

item.title: Sparse Analytic Representation of Stationary Processes with Bounded Spectral Density
item.description: arXiv:2611.27152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider centered second-order stationary processes Y={Y_t}{t\in R} with bounded spectral density S_Y and develop a sparse analytic representation framework. A nontrivial stationary process on the real line generally does not belong to L^2(\Omega,L^2(R)), since stationarity implies E||Y||{L^2(R)}^2=\infty. To overcome this infinite-energy obstruction, we replace the sample-path viewpoint by the bounded linear operator \widetilde Y: L^2(R) \to L^2(\Omega), with \widetilde Y(f) = \int_{R} \hat{f}(\xi) Z_Y(d\xi), where Z_Y is the orthogonal random measure in the spectral representation of Y. Applying \widetilde Y to Cauchy kernels in the upper and lower half-planes yields random analytic functions U_+ and U_-. For \alpha>1, we prove U_+ \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha^2(C^+)) and U_- \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha^2(C^-)), where B_\alpha^2(C^\pm) are weighted Bergman spaces. We combine U_+ and U_- into U(\omega,z) = U_+ for z \in C^+, and U_- for z \in C^-, and with B_\alpha = B_\alpha^2(C^+) \oplus B_\alpha^2(C^-), prove U \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha). We establish boundary vanishing, energy identity, and convergence, and derive covariance identities for the coefficients. In L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha), we apply stochastic pre-orthogonal adaptive Fourier decomposition (SPOAFD) to U_+ and U_- separately, using normalized reproducing kernels of the Bergman spaces as dictionaries. The adaptive selection is determined by the spectral density. Finally, using the Poisson kernel and SPOAFD expansions, we establish weak mean-square convergence of the original process against test functions in C_c^\infty(R).
item.dc:creator: Yiqiao Zhang, Fang Yang, Tao Qian

item.title: Finite Angular Derivative Sets and Almost Isometries of the Hyperbolic Disc
item.description: arXiv:2611.27387v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a subset $E$ of the unit circle is the set of points at which an analytic self-map of the unit disc has a finite angular derivative if and only if $E$ is an $F_\sigma$ set. We also prove that, for every countable dense subset $E$ of the unit circle, there exists an almost isometry in the sense of Garnett--Papadimitrakis whose angular derivative is finite precisely on $E$.
item.dc:creator: Angel Lorenzo

item.title: $L^p-L^q$ estimates for maximal operators associated to families of finite type curves
item.description: arXiv:1702.06754v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) boundedness of maximal operators associated with averages over families of finite-type curves in the plane. These operators are defined by \[ \mathbb{M}f(x):=\sup_{1\leq t\leq 2} \left|\int_{\mathbb{C}}f(x-ty)\rho(y)\,d\sigma(y)\right|, \] where \(d\sigma\) denotes the normalized Lebesgue measure on the curve \(\mathbb{C}\), and \(\rho\) is a smooth cutoff function. Let \(\triangle\) denote the closed triangle with vertices \[ P=\left(\frac25,\frac15\right),\qquad Q=\left(\frac12,\frac12\right),\qquad R=(0,0). \] We establish that, whenever \[ \left(\frac1p,\frac1q\right) \in \bigl(\triangle\setminus\{P,Q\}\bigr) \cap \left\{ \left(\frac1p,\frac1q\right): \frac1p<\frac2q,\quad p>\frac{(m+1)q}{q+1} \right\}, \] there exists a constant \(B>0\) such that \[ \|\mathbb{M}f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^2)} \leq B\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)}. \] As an application, we derive \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) estimates for solutions of higher-order strictly hyperbolic pseudodifferential equations.
item.dc:creator: Ramesh Manna

item.title: A characterization of compactness via bilinear $T1$ theorem
item.description: arXiv:2404.14013v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we develop the bilinear $T1$ theorem to characterize the (weighted) compactness of bilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operators. Let $T$ be a bilinear operator associated with a standard bilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund kernel. We prove that $T$ can be extended to a compact bilinear operator from $L^{p_1}(w_1^{p_1}) \times L^{p_2}(w_2^{p_2})$ to $L^p(w^p)$ for all exponents $\frac1p = \frac{1}{p_1} + \frac{1}{p_2}>0$ with $p_1, p_2 \in (1, \infty]$ and for all weights $(w_1, w_2) \in A_{(p_1, p_2)}$ if and only if the following hypotheses hold: (H1) $T$ is associated with a compact bilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund kernel, (H2) $T$ satisfies the weak compactness property, and (H3) $T(1,1), T^{*1}(1,1), T^{*2}(1,1) \in \mathrm{CMO}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. This is also equivalent to the endpoint compactness: (1) $T$ is compact from $L^1(w_1) \times L^1(w_2)$ to $L^{\frac12, \infty}(w^{\frac12})$ for all $(w_1, w_2) \in A_{(1, 1)}$, or (2) $T$ is compact from $L^{\infty}(w_1^{\infty}) \times L^{\infty}(w_2^{\infty})$ to $\mathrm{CMO}_{\lambda}(w^{\infty})$ for all $(w_1, w_2) \in A_{(\infty, \infty)}$. Besides, any of these properties is equivalent to the fact that $T$ admits a compact bilinear dyadic representation. Our main approaches consist of the following new ingredients: (i) a resulting representation of a compact bilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operator as an average of some compact bilinear dyadic shifts and paraproducts; (ii) extrapolation of endpoint compactness for bilinear operators; and (iii) compactness criterion in weighted Lorentz spaces. Finally, to illustrate the applicability of our result, we demonstrate the hypotheses (H1)-(H3) through examples including bilinear continuous/dyadic paraproducts, bilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear commutators.
item.dc:creator: Mingming Cao, Honghai Liu, Zengyan Si, K\^oz\^o Yabuta

item.title: The Ultra-Radical: Analytic Continuation, Branching, and Stability of the Principal Branch
item.description: arXiv:2512.18643v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the ultra-radical $\sqrt[{n;a;b}]{x}$, the multi-valued solution to $y^{a}=1+a x y^{b}$. Inside the convergence radius $|x|<R$, every branch is given by a Master-J power series; for $|x|\ge R$, analytic continuation requires switching to one of two conjugate series. We introduce a deterministic geometric criterion that selects, for each branch index $n$, the correct conjugate series, thereby eliminating heuristic search and guaranteeing branch continuity across $|x|=R$. Key finding: Only the principal branch ($n=0$) remains continuous when the parameters $a$, $b$, and $x$ vary smoothly. This includes the critical limits $a\to0$ (transition to an exponential equation) and $b\to0$ (transition to a binomial root), where the principal branch converges to the corresponding classical solution. In contrast, branches with $n\neq0$ exhibit oscillatory divergence as $a\to0$ and lose their identity in these limits. This structural continuity singles out the principal branch for applications where parameters may vary with the system's state, such as in nonlinear media with field-dependent exponents or adaptive dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Viktorovich Berezin

item.title: Why Directly Learning Periodic Trajectories Can Fail
item.description: arXiv:2609.32254v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Operator learning of periodic solutions requires deciding how simulation data should be recorded and represented. A natural choice is to integrate long enough for transients to decay and record a window wide enough to contain at least one full period of all trajectories. We find that these conservative choices can make the resulting trajectories difficult to learn, even when the underlying periodic orbits vary regularly with system parameters. Unaligned trajectories generalize poorly even within the training distribution. Phase alignment substantially improves in-distribution generalization, but models trained on a fixed physical-time window still have large errors on trajectories with periods outside the training range. We explain both failures through a common mechanism: frequency differences accumulate over time, so the target phase varies rapidly with the parameters. Predictors that cannot track this variation incur a population MSE floor in both settings; for fixed window prediction, we also derive a per-sample lower bound. We then study one of the simplest representations that escape these floors: learning an aligned, normalized waveform and its period separately. We establish regularity of the decoupled targets under ODE assumptions and show experimentally that this approach avoids both failures in ODE systems and a PDE case study.
item.dc:creator: Kaixin Zheng, Anita Layton

item.title: Decoupling and Tail Laws for Small-Order Metric-Valued Nonlocal Energies: A Structural View of the Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova Formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.01958v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for small-order limits of nonlocal energies with metric-valued maps. For globally $L^p$ maps, we consider interaction measures whose marginals have uniformly bounded $L^\infty$ densities $a_\alpha$ and $b_\alpha$. If these densities converge weakly-* to $a_\infty$ and $b_\infty$, the normalized energies converge to the $L^p$ energy weighted by $a_\infty+b_\infty$ if and only if the interaction measures escape every bounded rectangle. For maps that are only locally $L^p$, we introduce target laws describing the distribution of the values sampled at infinity. Convergence of their $p$-distance profiles yields the limiting interaction energy for every $1\leq p<\infty$ and arbitrary Polish targets, with integrated $p$-Wasserstein convergence as a sufficient criterion. The arguments include the endpoint $p=1$ and require no linear structure on the target space. Applications include directional and anisotropic Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova formulas, a Bernoulli-law interpretation of fractional perimeters, and an Abelian principle for heat-semigroup energies.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Pinamonti
